summary: Iteration 2: Multi-template support (bw_informative 1080x1350 + standard 1080x1080), channel name ANI, no '@' handle. All 10 backend pytest tests passed (templates list, settings-no-handle, create standard post with PIL dimension verification, PUT template switch re-renders at correct dimensions both directions, invalid template -> 422, cleanup). Only 1 POST /api/posts call executed (AI budget respected). Frontend Playwright flow validated: login, Settings page has no handle field and no '@' anywhere, brand_name default ANI, New Story page has both new-template-bw_informative and new-template-standard buttons with active state, Dashboard shows template label on card ('STANDARD · 4 SLIDES'), Review page has template-option-bw_informative and template-option-standard, template-changed-hint appears on switch, SlidePreview renders a 1080x1080 image uncropped (natural 1080x1080, box 456x456 square), preview caption begins with 'ANI ' (no '@'), ANI logo visible in top-right corner of rendered slide.
critical_code_review_comments: render.py std_slide: 'oswald' variable font Bold weight is set via set_variation_by_name — Oswald.ttf must be a variable font with 'Bold' name; verified working at runtime.
server.py edit_post: SettingsIn no longer has 'handle' field; PostEdit requires 'template' with default 'bw_informative'. Validation on unknown template returns 422 correctly.
Review.jsx preview uses w-full h-auto so both 1:1 and 4:5 render uncropped — good.
Dashboard card template label implemented with inline ternary (p.template === 'standard' ? 'Standard' : 'B&W'); won't scale if more templates added — low priority.
seed_data_creation: One post created via POST /api/posts (template=standard) during pytest run; deleted at end. Pre-existing 'standard' post in DB (Jantar Mantar) was used read-only by frontend flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file is pytest-based and reusable. Note: /api/media fetch can be slow (storage proxy); use timeout>=60s. Rendered URLs returned by API are relative paths like '/api/media/...' — prefix with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL to fetch. Previous iteration note that URLs 'start with http' was incorrect — they are relative; frontend SlidePreview prefixes with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no failures. Initial backend run surfaced two self-inflicted test issues: (1) rendered URLs are relative paths, not absolute; (2) /api/media fetch exceeded 30s default. Fixed in test file by prefixing BASE_URL and bumping timeout to 90s.
